solution:
We know that the angle opposite to the largest side of a triangle is the largest angle of the triangle.
Here side \(AB\) (\(= c\)) is the largest side, so \(C\) is the largest angle. We show \(C\) is obtuse.
\(\cos C = \dfrac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} = \dfrac{2^2 + 3^2 - 4^2}{2(2)(3)} = \dfrac{-3}{12} = -\dfrac{1}{4}\).
As \(\cos C\) is negative, \(C\) is an obtuse angle.
\(\therefore \triangle ABC\) is an obtuse angled triangle.
note: 2ab = 2(2)(3) = 12, printed 2(3)(4) = 24: cos C = -1/4, not -1/8. Still negative, so the conclusion stands.

solution:
We have \(\sec\theta + \sqrt{2} = 0\) \(\therefore \cos\theta = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\)
\(\therefore \cos\theta = \cos\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\) \(\left(\text{As } \cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \text{ and } \cos(\pi - A) = -\cos A\right)\)
The general solution of \(\cos\theta = \cos\alpha\) is \(\theta = 2n\pi \pm \alpha\), where \(n \in Z\).
\(\therefore\) The general solution of \(\cos\theta = \cos\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\) is \(\theta = 2n\pi \pm \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\), where \(n \in Z\).
\(\therefore\) The general solution of \(\sec\theta = -\sqrt{2}\) is \(\theta = 2n\pi \pm \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\), where \(n \in Z\).
note: The equation is sec theta = -sqrt 2 (printed +sqrt 2); the general solution 2n pi +- 3 pi/4 stands.
